question: What is the main purpose of handover documentation in midwifery?

options.A: To punish staff who make clinical errors on duty
options.B: To ensure continuity of care between shift changes
options.C: To replace verbal communication entirely in the ward
options.D: To provide strict billing records for the hospital

explanation: Handover documentation guarantees that crucial patient details are safely passed to the next team to keep care continuous and safe. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is a clear handover vital when managing a woman in active labor?

options.A: It stops the doctor from asking questions during ward rounds
options.B: Labor progress can change rapidly requiring immediate coordinated action
options.C: Midwives on the incoming shift refuse to read long patient histories
options.D: Hospital management requires a signed form every single hour

explanation: Active labor is dynamic, and the incoming team must know the exact status to act fast if complications arise. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective documentation?

options.A: Labor pain is too much for this young woman
options.B: Blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and pulse is 72
options.C: Mother seems very happy with her new baby
options.D: Patient is fine and sleeping comfortably now

explanation: Objective documentation relies on measurable facts and numbers rather than personal opinions or vague descriptions. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h2)

question: When is the best time for a midwife to write clinical notes during a shift?

options.A: At the very end of the shift from memory
options.B: During the morning handover meeting with doctors
options.C: As close to the actual event or observation as possible
options.D: Only when the unit manager asks to check the files

explanation: Writing notes immediately prevents memory lapses and ensures the record reflects the true timeline of care. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h2)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication framework?
explanation: In the SBAR tool, B stands for Background, which covers the past medical and obstetric history relevant to the current admission. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h3)

question: A midwife tells the incoming shift: 'Postpartum mother in bed three has a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg.' Which part of SBAR is this?
explanation: Current vital signs and clinical findings form part of the Assessment section of SBAR. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the proper way to correct a writing mistake in a paper patient record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the whole nursing note
options.B: Draw a single neat line through it, write the correction, sign and date
options.C: Scratch out the error heavily until it cannot be read at all
options.D: Apply liquid correction fluid and write over the clean space

explanation: A single line keeps the original entry readable, which protects the legal integrity of the document. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why are clinical handover notes considered legal documents?

options.A: They are printed on special paper approved by the police
options.B: They can be used as evidence in a court of law if questions arise
options.C: They must be stamped by a government lawyer before filing
options.D: They belong to the hospital owner rather than the patient

explanation: Patient records stand as legal proof of the care delivered by the healthcare team. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe documentation practice?

options.A: Reporting specific vital signs instead of writing 'normal'
options.B: Documenting a procedure before you actually perform it
options.C: Signing your full name and title next to every entry
options.D: Writing patient notes immediately after finishing a procedure

explanation: Charting care before it happens is dangerous because plans can change suddenly, leading to false records. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is leaving large blank spaces in a paper handover book discouraged?

options.A: It makes the handover book look untidy during rounds
options.B: Someone could write unauthorized entries into the gap later
options.C: The hospital auditor will fine the ward for poor spacing
options.D: It wastes valuable stationery meant for other patients

explanation: Blank spaces compromise security because fraudulent notes could be squeezed in after the shift ends. [learn more](BMP115_U4_T8#BMP115_U4_T8_h5)
